findings: The §3 'plate ii — nine of my faces' image is muddy and low-contrast: the layered ghosted 'André Macedo' lettering reads as noise rather than legible composition, the weakest tile on the page.
The exposure table (1 / 3 / 6 / 9 with '26 / 25–26 / 14–26 / 5–26') is on-theme but its numeric logic is opaque and verges on decoration-as-data.
The right-hand body block under §1 ('I have been rebuilt 256 times…') floats in isolation with a lot of dead space around it; its placement feels less resolved than the strong left-column rag.
The metaphor density (plates, arcs, telos AI narration) is heavy — the poetic metadata strip at the very top risks reading as filler to a visitor who only wants name/role/contact.
what_works: High-contrast Didone display ('André Macedo') set against a mono utility caption voice is a genuine, sustained typographic point of view — the opposite of default-sans slop.

The hero is a deliberate system, not a centered headline: top-left name, dark navy field, and a real long-exposure orange light-arc photograph on the right, with the whole 'light painting / plate held open' conceit carried consistently through every section.

Asymmetric editorial composition — numbered sections (§1–§5), mono sidebars, a generative radial star-trail graphic, and the cream-paper body against the dark hero — uses whitespace as compositional mass with real tension.
Color is disciplined: near-black/navy and warm cream governed by a single amber accent used only on italic emphasis words and key numerals, never as rainbow garnish.
A.reasoning: This is not a SaaS template: it rejects every cardinal slop state — no centered hero, no purple gradient, no three-card row, no default sans — in favor of a committed Didone-vs-mono editorial system wrapped around a coherent long-exposure/plate metaphor and a photographic hero. Composition is asymmetric and intentional, type craft is the strongest axis, and the stranger test clears the floor: name, two-company role line, and a visible me@andremacedo.com all read in the first viewport. Minor weaknesses (a muddy plate-ii image and a slightly opaque exposure table) keep it from the top band but it comfortably clears threshold.

findings: multiple competing focal points across long vertical scroll (hero light painting, historical text blocks, data tables, spiral diagram all pull equal attention without clear single entry point per viewport)
some ad-hoc type sizing rather than a strict modular scale (headline sizes feel intuitive but not rigorously ratio-based)
occasional safe centered text blocks and symmetrical data tables that border on default editorial layout patterns
what_works: decisive conceptual move of framing the entire site as a living photographic plate/long-exposure artifact with consistent 'plate' numbering, timestamps, and light-painting metaphor
strong hero light-trail arch against night sky with precise typographic overlay and location metadata creates memorable, non-generic first impression
expressive pairing of elegant serif for body with structured tabular data and technical mono elements; restrained warm amber/orange accent against deep navy and off-white
the spiral 'star trail' diagram and interactive plate elements deliver a signature visual language that a templated generator would not produce
B.reasoning: This is not SaaS-landing slop or generic centered-hero template. The living 'long exposure plate' conceit is executed with conviction across typography, color, and custom diagrams (light painting spiral, overlaid name plate, path-over-Miami). Hero is the strongest element with its decisive light-trail composition. Type craft and color show clear point of view. However, the very long scroll dilutes focal hierarchy with many equally-weighted sections, and some internal blocks fall into conventional editorial rhythm rather than pushing the metaphor further. Stranger_test passes easily in the first viewport. Overall a strong but not flawless execution that earns above the midline but not excellence on every axis.
